subject: Batching pnly when a resource becomes available

messages.author: bf65c0e4657848f5
messages.subject: Batching pnly when a resource becomes available
parts:
Is it possible to batch when a resource becomes available?

For example, you have two or more different types of objects queueing for a single process. The process can handle 4 at a time, but only a single type of object can run in each load.

Batching presents issues because if I use the timeout function, if a similar object joins the queue it isn't added to the batch after the batch occurs. 

I would like items to batch based on the object that has been queueing the longest, taking any like items in the queue with it (FIFO while utilizing all available capacity). Is it possible to batch one batch at a time right before the batch goes through the process?

I don't think that batching is an option here, because batches block
arrivals and you don't want that. But I would need an example to
understand exactly what you are up to. Let's suppose we have the
following queue with arrivals of types A, B:

server <- A1, A2, A3, B1, A4, A5

How do you process them?

- A1, A2, A3, then B1, then A4, A5
- A1, A2, A3, A4, then B1, then A5
- A1, A2, A3, A4, then A5, then B1
- other?

Iñaki

messages.author: 0f5b7adb7e70bd8b
messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Batching pnly when a resource becomes available
parts:
On Tue, 26 Feb 2019 at 16:10, An Tal <a6m7...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> A1, A2, A3, A4, B1 A5

Then it's clear that you don't need batching, but a kind of custom
priority queue that changes dynamically. I think that this can be
achieved with simmer, but requires a careful design. You'll need, at
least, the following elements:

1) Every arrival must have a private attribute establishing the type or class.

2) The first arrival that seizes the empty server must set its type as
a global attribute, meaning that this type of arrival is being
processed.

3) Then you need to "rotate" the whole queue: the next arrival enters
the server, and the type is checked (this is obviously a branch). If
the type is the same, it continues and proceeds to the timeout
function; otherwise, it must release immediately and be inserted into
the queue again. This happens until the server is full or the whole
queue has been checked ("rotated").

4) To be able to re-insert arrivals, you need to increase the priority
(so that they are inserted before eventual new arrivals) and then
simply roll back to the seize activity.

5) But they can't roll back straight away, because it would cause an
infinite loop. They need to wait there until the server is released
(the trap-wait-send mechanism is ideal for this).

In fact, on second thought, if you don't set a maximum capacity for
the resource and instead you control this through the check in step
3), then you don't need to increase the priority in step 4), because
you don't even need the queue at all.

Iñaki
